data.narrative:
Dusty Robotics is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Tessa Lau and Philipp Herget that has raised $70M+. The valuation analysis draws from a broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector universe comprising nine private peers (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics) and one public comparable (277810.KQ).

Stage-progression analysis, the only methodologically sound approach given data constraints, applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement. Using a $4M proxy derived from the company's total capital raised, this method implies a valuation of $9M. The peer-median approach was not applicable; while ten same-sector peers exist, the filtered peer set (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than three) to support reliable median benchmarking. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $7M (low) to $10M (high), with a $9M median. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method and should be weighted accordingly. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the $4M raised proxy as a valuation anchor, the applicability of 2.5x stage advancement multipliers to this particular subsector, and the company's current capital structure. Additional traction metrics or comparable transaction data would materially narrow the range.
